name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,276

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pulse oddly weak with diamonds on display — no ecstasy

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd positions of the next word, first, third and so on
no says the following item is missing, so the drug's letter must be taken out

blocks.note: first and third letters of the word
an expo is an exhibition or display
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy
D is the card-playing abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A feeble heartbeat at a showy jewellery exhibition where nobody is on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'diamonds on display' puts the diamonds letter after the shortened exhibition word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wax pod is a yellow-podded kind of bean, and beans are pulses in the culinary and botanical sense.

clue.text: They’re hollow words often repeated without introduction

definitions.note: a clause standing for a plural noun: things that are hollow

indicators.note: lacking its introduction means the opening letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a mantra is a word or phrase chanted over and over

explanation.surface: A sneer at empty slogans that people keep reciting without any preamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They're hollow' looks like a comment on the words, but it is the definition: hollow cavities.
explanation.definitionFit: Antra is the plural of antrum, an anatomical cavity or sinus, so they are hollows in the body.

clue.text: Drug for bearing operation that makes me laugh

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the first word holds the next one inside it

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
an act is a deed or operation
the texting abbreviation for laughing out loud

explanation.surface: Someone wants a medicine for a surgical procedure that they find hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: PR(ACT)O + LOL.
explanation.definitionFit: Practolol is a beta-blocker formerly prescribed for heart rhythm problems, so it is a medicine.

clue.text: Ways in which lifts succeeded with a delivery

indicators.note: in a down entry, the letter abbreviating succeeded is lifted, rising above its neighbour

blocks.note: doors are ways in to a building
taken as written

explanation.surface: A note on lift doors in a building that worked, plus something delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the usual abbreviation for succeeded, and the S at the end of the doors climbs one place before the A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A doosra is a cricket ball bowled by an off-spinner that turns the opposite way, one kind of bowled delivery.

clue.text: Old chap at home with iron bed: that French article

definitions.text: Old chap at home with iron

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed
que is French for that
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An elderly man at home with a bedstead, followed by some French grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with iron' seems to describe the bed, but it belongs to the definition: a man doing the ironing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotquean is an archaic term for a man who busies himself with household chores thought of as women's work.

clue.text: Cracking the old cryptic? Nothing to Mark, applying light to cells

indicators.note: cracking breaks things apart, so the words that follow are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
O is a standard abbreviation for old
taken as written
zero, nothing, looks like the letter O
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for the old German mark

anagrams.fodder: THE O CRYPTIC O TO M

explanation.surface: A solver solving an old-fashioned puzzle finds nothing worth marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Cytophotometric describes measuring cell contents by passing light through stained cells, so it involves shining light on cells.

clue.text: Preservative’s function settled by hospital

blocks.note: tan is the abbreviation for tangent, a trigonometric function
alit is a past tense of alight, to settle or land
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: The role of a preservative is decided by a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanalith is a trade name for a copper-based chemical treatment pressure-injected into timber to protect it from rot.

clue.text: Daughter replacing last pair of pants, maybe ruined

indicators.note: the first item takes the place of the final two letters of the word that follows

blocks.note: pants, in the British sense of underpants, are one kind of undies
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter swapping out the last two pairs of her trousers, which may have been spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: D replaces the ES of UNDIES. In Britain pants means underpants, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo something is to wreck or destroy it, so undid works as the past-tense verb ruined.

clue.text: Area, one I must confess includes dock for sugar producer

indicators.note: includes means takes in, so the confession holds the next word within it

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
a wrongdoing of mine that I need to own up to
to dock a tail is to lop it

explanation.surface: A confession about a wrongdoing involving a harbour, made in a sugar-refining district.
explanation.walkthrough: A + MY(LOP)SIN: 'dock' suggests a harbour but is the verb meaning cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Amylopsin is the pancreatic enzyme that breaks starch down into maltose, so it produces a sugar.

clue.text: Seat that folds back in unit, no part separate

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the letters are read from right to left
in says the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: read backwards across the words, from the S of separate to the start of unit

explanation.surface: A folding seat built as a single unit, with no part to detach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folds back' reads naturally as one phrase, but 'folds' belongs to the definition and 'back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A strapontin is a folding tip-up seat, as found in French theatres and taxis, so it is a seat designed to fold.

clue.text: Light opera singer’s very in need of a supporting line

indicators.text: in need of a supporting line
indicators.note: a letter given an upright stroke underneath to prop it up changes shape into a different letter

blocks.note: a diva is a leading female opera singer
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A comic-opera soprano is badly in need of a line to prop her up.
explanation.walkthrough: The V in DIVA, given a vertical stroke beneath it, becomes a Y. 'Light opera' looks like one phrase, but Light is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A diya is a small clay oil lamp lit in India, notably at Diwali, so it is a source of light.

clue.text: Plant that’s busy bringing in key personnel

indicators.note: bringing in means taking something inside, so the first word surrounds the following ones

blocks.note: a busy is old British slang for a police officer, as is cop
Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
HR, human resources, is the personnel department

explanation.surface: A busy factory is hiring important staff.
explanation.walkthrough: C(ALT HR)OP. 'Plant' reads as a factory, and 'busy' as an adjective, but busy is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: Calthrop is a variant spelling of caltrop, the name of several prickly-fruited plants such as the water chestnut.

clue.text: Ball enjoyed by Indians put on in smallest room

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: the smallest room is a British euphemism for the toilet, the loo
to put on is to add

explanation.surface: A dance held for Indian guests is staged in the tiniest room in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' suggests a dance or a cricket ball, but it is a round sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A laddoo is a round Indian sweet made from flour, sugar and ghee, a ball-shaped treat popular in South Asia.

clue.text: Bloke releasing cry of pain collapsed

indicators.note: releasing means letting go of something, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: a fellow is a man or chap
the exclamation of someone hurt

explanation.surface: A man who lets out a yelp of pain and keels over.
explanation.definitionFit: Fell is the past tense of fall, so it means toppled over or went down, just as collapsed does.

clue.text: Movement for peace I run that makes for good living

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for one who goes after good living

indicators.note: movement means the letters shift position, so the following words are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who runs a peace campaign that leads to a comfortable life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement for peace' looks like an anti-war campaign, but Movement is only the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is a person devoted to fine food, drink and pleasure, one who heads for the sensual comforts of life.

clue.text: Shoot puck mostly wildly in hockey game

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped
wildly means in an unruly, disordered way, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Advice to a hockey player to fire the puck at goal with abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Octopush is the British name for underwater hockey, played on a pool floor with short sticks and a weighted puck.

clue.text: Everything’s flowing from container: viscous stuff that is hard to lift

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting something reads it from bottom to top

blocks.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
tar is a thick, sticky liquid
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Thick sticky liquid pours out of a pot, and it is heavy to pick up.
explanation.definitionFit: Panta rhei is the Greek saying attributed to Heraclitus that all things are in flux, meaning everything is in motion.

clue.text: State without borders within small island recalled part of W Germany once

indicators.note: without its borders, the word loses its outermost letters at each end
recalled means called back, so the word is read in the opposite direction
within puts the first item inside the second

blocks.note: an ait is a small island in a river
Arizona is a US state

explanation.surface: A borderless state set on a little island, remembered as a section of West Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: The island is reversed first, then the trimmed state goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trizonia was the name for the combined American, British and French occupation zones of post-war Germany before 1949.

clue.text: Judge one’s going to regret eavesdropping on a farm trainee down under

indicators.note: an eavesdropper only hears things, so the word is given by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge
I'll, short for I will, says the speaker is going to
taken as written
to rue is to regret, and the sound is spelt as the Australian kangaroo

explanation.surface: A judge expecting remorse after listening in on a young Australian farmhand.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on a' puts the sound-alike after the A, not before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jillaroo is an Australian term for a young woman training as a station hand on a sheep or cattle station.

clue.text: Needing a party to back, one which will bear fruit

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the phrase is read from end to start

blocks.note: to be in on something is to be a party to it

explanation.surface: Someone needs a political party behind them, and one that will deliver results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a party' looks like a political party or celebration, but 'a party to' is a whole phrase meaning involved in.
explanation.definitionFit: Noni is a small tropical tree of the coffee family, Morinda citrifolia, grown for its pungent edible fruit.

clue.text: Beneath Asian peak in the past, dread tailless creatures nearby?

indicators.note: without a tail, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: K1 was the survey name once used for Masherbrum in the Karakoram, with the 1 read as I
angst is dread or anxiety

explanation.surface: Under a Himalayan summit long ago, fear of animals lurking close by.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'Beneath' puts the dread below the peak. The question mark flags that 'nearby' means near that Asian peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiangs are wild asses native to the Tibetan plateau, so they are animals living near the Karakoram mountains.

clue.text: Direction for those accompanying quartet into canal

indicators.note: into places the first item inside the second

blocks.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea
IV is the Roman numeral for four

explanation.surface: Instructions for people escorting four travellers through a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: SU(IV)EZ. 'Direction' sounds like steering a boat, but here it is a musical instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Suivez, French for follow, is a musical instruction telling accompanists to follow the soloist's tempo.

clue.text: Ducks going north on journey, commonly

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means travelling upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

blocks.note: ducks and luv are both northern English terms of endearment, like dear
to go is to travel or journey

explanation.surface: Wild ducks heading north on their usual migration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' looks like birds, but it is the friendly northern English address 'ducks', meaning love.
explanation.definitionFit: Vulgo is a Latin adverb meaning in the vulgar tongue, used to introduce the everyday name for something.

clue.text: English private detective rank that can effect a downward curve?

definitions.text: that can effect a downward curve?
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: something that causes a downward curve

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
PI is short for private investigator
rank means foul or nasty

explanation.surface: An English sleuth of low standing who can bend his rivals' careers downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rank' suggests a position in a hierarchy, but it is the adjective meaning foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Epinasty is the downward bending of a leaf or petal caused by faster growth on its upper side.

clue.text: Exercise, with time again for second canter

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands where another was

blocks.note: a sit-up is a stomach exercise
T is the abbreviation for time
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A workout where the time is used again for a second ride on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: T replaces the S of SITUP; 'again' notes that the word already has one T.
explanation.definitionFit: To titup is to prance or move with a bouncy, lively gait, as a horse does at an easy canter.

clue.text: Wicket to be found to turn for Yorkshire spinner?

indicators.note: turning round means the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: W is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for wicket
to lie somewhere is to be found there

explanation.surface: A wicket that turns, ideal for a Yorkshire spin bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: W + EIL. 'Yorkshire spinner' suggests a cricketer, but it is a dialect word for something that spins.
explanation.definitionFit: Weil is a northern dialect word for a whirlpool, water that spins around, hence a regional spinner.

clue.text: Criminals nicked on vacation called hotel when expected

indicators.note: vacated means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word stay

blocks.note: first and last letters only
rang means telephoned or called
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ETA is short for estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: Crooks arrested while on holiday phoned their hotel to say when they'd arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'Ndrangheta is the Calabrian mafia, a powerful organised crime syndicate based in southern Italy.

clue.text: What might have one piece per member country, not conforming to certain law

definitions.text: What might have one piece per member country

blocks.clueFragment: What might have one piece per member country
blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: a picture of the United Nations made of tiles, one per nation
second meaning: outside the law of Moses

explanation.walkthrough: Split as UN MOSAIC, it is a mosaic of the United Nations, one tile per member state.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosaic law is the law given to Moses, so something un-Mosaic does not follow those biblical commandments.

clue.text: Work from the East applied to vessel?

definitions.text: Work from the East applied to vessel?

indicators.note: coming from the East in an across entry means travelling right to left, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a ship is a sea-going vessel
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A piece of oriental craftsmanship fixed onto a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: SHIP + PO. Read whole, the clue also defines the answer: Japanese enamelling put on vases.
explanation.definitionFit: Shippo is Japanese cloisonné enamel ware, a decorative technique from the Far East used on vases and bowls.
